title: 制御系プログラミング
subtitle: Programming for control systems
keywords: Programming 2.Numerical computation 3.Control system simulation 4.Frequency analysis 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Understand how physical phenomena can be modeled using differential equations and analyzed with computers. (2) Acquire the ability to implement numerical computation algorithms and perform analyses through programming. (3) Develop the ability to interpret analytical results and improve programs for higher accuracy.
advice: This course introduces mathematical models used to represent physical phenomena and provides training in numerical computation methods using MATLAB/Simulink. Students will learn how to construct models (block diagrams) and perform control system simulations. Topics include: Programming using MATLAB 1. Numerical computation with MATLAB (basic operations and matrix calculations) 2. Vibration analysis using MATLAB (differential equations; spring–mass–damper models) 3. Signal processing using MATLAB (FFT: Fast Fourier Transform) 4. Control system analysis using MATLAB (transfer functions, Bode plots, transient response) 5. Control system design using Simulink (transient response, PID control) Classes will be conducted primarily through exercises. Students are expected to prepare adequately before each class.
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to have a basic understanding of MATLAB usage as learned in the introductory AI course. Knowledge of programming languages such as C or Python is desirable. Concurrent enrollment in Control Engineering (required) and Mechanical Dynamics II (elective), which supports understanding of vibration models, is recommended.

activityGoals.body: Be able to develop programs for input/output operations and numerical calculations.
Be able to solve differential equations using numerical methods.
Be able to perform frequency analysis using numerical computation.
Be able to plot transient responses and Bode diagrams for mechanical models.
Be able to simulate and evaluate system responses from control block diagrams.
Be able to develop and apply programs to solve problems in mechanical engineering.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Be able to design and implement efficient and well-structured programs. (2) Be able to select appropriate methods considering error and stability. (3) Be able to interpret frequency characteristics considering analysis conditions. (4)Be able to explain how parameter changes affect dynamic characteristics. (5)Be able to adjust and improve system performance based on results. (6) Be able to formulate problems algorithmically and apply solutions broadly.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Be able to create programs for basic input/output processing and numerical calculations. (2) Be able to solve differential equations using common numerical methods. (3) Be able to obtain frequency spectra using FFT. (4) Be able to generate transient responses and Bode diagrams and identify basic characteristics. (5) Be able to simulate system responses and evaluate performance. (6) Be able to develop programs to analyze mechanical engineering problems.
